extraction.summary: The authors propose that matter exchanges energy with hidden quantum-gravity defect degrees of freedom, so unimodular gravity's geometric cosmological constant becomes dynamical. They reduce a matter scalar plus oscillator bath to a Langevin equation; an ideal Ohmic kernel makes friction local, requires a divergent mass counterterm, and proposes a diffusion law for Lambda, although Sol found unresolved printed Hamiltonian normalization conflicts in Eq.(29). In the illustrative noiseless branch, a homogeneous massless scalar has p=rho (stiff matter, not radiation); for positive dimensionless gamma and initial Lambda_d=0, first-order perturbation theory predicts a monotonic rise to Lambda_infinity=gamma m_p H_d/2. Figure 1 shows one numerical example. These are conditional results of a symmetry-reduced toy model with a low-excitation initial bath, not a fit, observation, demonstration of a quantum-gravity microphysics, or completion of a causal-set fluctuating-Lambda model.

ideas.title: In unimodular gravity, matter non-conservation sources a spacetime-dependent geometric Lambda
ideas.description: The trace-free field equation plus the integrability condition dJ=0 lets the authors rewrite the equations as Einstein equations with a cosmological term Lambda=Lambda_0+integral J. In flat FLRW, the cosmic-time Friedmann and continuity equations contain geometric Lambda and an energy exchange term; a Raychaudhuri equation leaves only two independent equations for a(tau), rho(tau) and Lambda(tau). A diffusion law is therefore required to close the homogeneous background. Lambda has geometric units (inverse length squared); its associated energy density is Lambda/(8 pi G).

equations.conventions_definitions: J is the diffusion current; dJ=0 is the integrability condition; the path integral from a reference event is path independent under that condition.
equations.domain: Unimodular gravity with non-conserved matter stress energy; Lambda is a geometric cosmological term.

ideas.title: A matter-coupled Ohmic oscillator bath produces local damping and a dynamical dark-energy term
ideas.description: The authors impose the unimodular lapse N=a^-3, so their Hamiltonian time is t with dt=a^3 d tau and v=a^3. They add a defect Hamiltonian H_D that is independent of v and p_v, coupling it to matter but not directly to the low-energy geometry; they warn that arbitrary modifications made only after symmetry reduction need not respect four-dimensional covariance. The defects are harmonic oscillators linearly coupled to a scalar. Eliminating them gives a memory kernel beta and noise xi. The Ohmic delta-kernel beta(t-t')=bar_beta m_p delta(t-t') makes dissipation local; beta(0) is divergent and is absorbed by M_0^2-beta(0)=M^2 with finite non-negative M. On shell, the displayed Hamiltonian counterterm delta Lambda and Eq. (31) define an effective Lambda=Lambda_0+delta Lambda. Equation (33) explicitly retains the noise cross-correlation term. Sol source amendment: the printed Eqs.(28)-(33) are not a consistent derivation as written; Eq.(29) has density/geometric-Lambda and friction-factor conflicts. No repair adopted.

ideas.title: Positive Ohmic transfer generates a positive late-time Lambda in a conditional stiff-matter background
ideas.description: The paper drops xi when solving the background, explicitly interpreting this as a sufficiently unexcited initial defect bath/low-entropy big bang assumption. Converting Eq. (33) to cosmic time gives Lambda'/8 pi G=bar_beta m_p (rho+p)a^-3. The illustrative M=0 homogeneous scalar has p=rho, so it is stiff matter (w=1), not radiation. With gamma=2 bar_beta/a_d^3, initial Lambda(tau_d)=0, rho(tau_d)=rho_d, and small gamma, the first-order solution approaches Lambda_infinity=gamma m_p H_d/2 over a timescale of order H_d^-1. This monotonic positive branch is not asserted to complete or replace causal-set fluctuating-Lambda models.

equations.domain: Homogeneous flat-FLRW background under the Ohmic model.

equations.conventions_definitions: a_d=a(tau_d) at diffusion onset; the equations depend on a_d/a, not an independently meaningful normalization of a. A homogeneous massless scalar has p=rho, not the radiation equation of state p=rho/3.
equations.domain: Small-gamma perturbative example with a homogeneous massless scalar; not a radiation-fluid solution.

ideas.title: The defect bath supplies a classical fluctuation-dissipation noise term whose initial temperature affects the background
ideas.description: Appendix A explicitly specifies a random equipartition initial bath at temperature T_d, gives zero-mean noise and its autocorrelation, and derives the Ohmic white-noise covariance. It then solves the late-time massless-field Langevin equation, explicitly calculates both <phi_dot^2> and the cross-correlation <xi phi_dot>, and uses them in Eq. (33) to claim equilibrium rho=T_d^4. The main-text noiseless solution is therefore a low-excitation/cold-bath branch, not an omission of the noise correlation. A reader algebra check finds that the displayed averages and Eq. (33) instead imply rho=T_d^4/2; the printed mismatch is unresolved, not repaired here. The appendix also calls the equilibrated matter radiation, while the homogeneous massless scalar defined by Eq. (30) has p=rho.

assumptions: The background is spatially flat FLRW and homogeneous, and the matter sector is represented by one minimally coupled scalar field.
The hidden defect Hamiltonian couples only to matter and is independent of the geometric phase-space variables v and p_v; this is the authors' minimal symmetry-compatible restriction.

The oscillator bath can be approximated as an ideal Ohmic continuum with beta(t-t')=bar_beta m_p delta(t-t'); the ultraviolet mass divergence is absorbed by a counterterm, while no microscopic spectrum or cutoff is specified.

The main background solution neglects xi(t), assuming the initial bath is sufficiently unexcited at the big bang. This is a low-entropy/low-temperature branch, not a general consequence of the oscillator model.
The illustrative genesis result uses M=0, so the homogeneous scalar has p=rho (stiff matter), and assumes positive small gamma with Lambda(tau_d)=0 and rho(tau_d)=rho_d.
Equation (39) is perturbative in gamma while Lambda is subdominant; the authors say an intermediate regime needs numerical integration and that the late-time geometry tends to de Sitter.
caveats: The authors explicitly describe the defect oscillators as a toy model, not the actual Planckian constituents; the underlying quantum-gravity microphysics remains unknown.

The theory is only a homogeneous background treatment here: no perturbation closure, CMB calculation, structure-growth prediction, observational fit or independently reconstructed likelihood is provided.

The link between a chosen gamma and the observed dark-energy scale is not fixed. Lambda_infinity depends on the freely chosen onset density and coupling, and the bath initial state is also uncalibrated.

The main calculation sets the noise to zero using a cold/low-excitation initial-bath assumption. Appendix A explicitly includes xi autocorrelation and <xi phi_dot>; it says a Planck-temperature bath would instead make noise dominate and generate Planck-scale Lambda.

Source-internal unresolved normalization: PDF p. 8 gives <phi_dot^2>=2rho/(3 Lambda t^2), <xi phi_dot>=bar_beta m_p T_d^4/(3 Lambda t^2), and Eq. (33) as Lambda_dot/(8 pi G)=bar_beta m_p phi_dot^2-phi_dot xi. These displayed relations plus <Lambda_dot>=0 imply rho=T_d^4/2, while Eq. (A9) prints rho=T_d^4. The white-noise endpoint prescription is not stated; no repair is assumed. Eq. (A10) inherits this normalization uncertainty.

Appendix A calls the equilibrated component radiation, but the model's homogeneous M=0 scalar obeys p=rho in Eq. (30) and footnote 8, not the radiation equation of state. Preserve this wording as an unresolved source inconsistency.
The numerical curve in Fig. 1 confirms only the stated toy setup's plotted behavior; it is not independent reproduction or evidence for the physical existence of QG defects.

The paper's qualitative motivation from quantum-gravity discreteness does not establish ancestry, equivalence, or completion of the separately registered causal-set fluctuating/sign-changing Lambda model. That paper is not an explicit bibliography match here.

The transcription is faithful, but the chain is inconsistent: Eq.(28) adds deltaLambda/(8piG) to an energy-density Hamiltonian, Eq.(31) adds deltaLambda to geometric Lambda, yet Eq.(29) RHS has density units. Its derivative also has coefficient beta_bar m_p/2 rather than the beta_bar m_p in Eq.(33). Eq.(27) and scalar continuity support the coefficient/sign in Eq.(33); this is a diagnostic, not authority to rewrite Eq.(29). Keep the deterministic system conditional and the Hamiltonian normalization blocked.

Confirmed literally from displayed averages and Eq.(33): 0=beta_bar m_p(2rho-T_d^4)/(3Lambda t^2). This identifies the printed factor mismatch; rho=T_d^4/2 is not adopted as the physically repaired equilibrium. White-noise endpoint normalization, finite-cutoff limit and bath mode-sum measure are unspecified. Appendix A does calculate <xi phi_dot>, so omission of that correlation is not an objection. A nonzero constant equilibrium density would additionally require an expanding-background continuity check; the homogeneous scalar has p=rho, not radiation.
extraction.strongest_objection: The claimed late-time dark-energy generation depends on an uncalibrated toy bath and a deliberately low-excitation initial state, with no microscopic derivation of gamma or current-data/perturbation closure. More concretely, Appendix A's displayed fluctuation averages do not algebraically yield its claimed equilibrium density: Eq. (33) gives rho=T_d^4/2 from the printed <phi_dot^2> and <xi phi_dot>, whereas Eq. (A9) states rho=T_d^4. This leaves the finite-temperature equilibrium normalization, and thus the stated Eq. (A10) correction, unresolved. The main noiseless branch does not rely on claiming the correlation is absent; it relies on dropping noise as a cold/low-excitation assumption.
extraction.cheapest_decisive_check: Do a short source-level algebra audit of PDF p. 8: start from Eq. (30) with M=0 and Eq. (33), insert the displayed Appendix averages for <phi_dot^2> and <xi phi_dot>, and state the white-noise endpoint/stochastic convention used in evaluating Eq. (A8). Reconcile the factor needed for Eq. (A9) and propagate it to Eq. (A10), without changing the paper's printed result in the record. In the same check, keep the homogeneous scalar's p=rho separate from radiation p=rho/3. This is non-duplicative and requires no new cosmological data or numerical experiment.

usefulness.assessment: Strong reason to investigate: the paper derives a concrete matter-to-hidden-bath channel and a local Ohmic diffusion law instead of postulating a diffusion function, then supplies a simple conditional late-time Lambda solution that can be checked against its Hamiltonian, time conventions and noise treatment. It is scientifically useful as a source-development target, not as evidence that QG defects exist or that the observed dark-energy value is explained.
usefulness.best_follow_up: First resolve the Appendix A equilibrium normalization and its radiation-versus-stiff-scalar wording at source level. If those checks clarify the intended normalization, a separate Sol review can check the Hamiltonian signs, energy transfer, time conversion and overlap with already registered unimodular diffusion sources. Keep the causal-set fluctuating-Lambda line distinct; no completion or equivalence is asserted.
